finding: First exercise of DECISION-0052's rule that "an answer is not canonical until... the production grader awards it 100% against its own rubric". Of the 3 F items the QA grader path can reach, 2 fail — and both failures are grader defects, not content defects. In each case the grader's own decision_explanation affirms the criterion while its status returns unable_to_determine and awards 0, and the grader's own integrity checker flags the contradiction.
evidence: Run via app.qa_grade_frq (no-persist, all seven persistence flags false), grader gpt-4.1-mini, prompt v1.0.0, arm b, qa_path_version evaluate-attempt-qa-no-persist-2026-09-22. S-101: 3/4, status uncertain, confidence low, integrity_issues=[earned_points_mismatch on a-iv] — the answer states both halves the criterion requires (fewest character-state changes; fewest unsupported convergent assumptions). S-102: 4/4, graded, high, no integrity issues. S-103: 4/5, integrity_issues=[evidence_not_found on c-ii] while its own explanation reads "gives a valid reason molecular data is more reliable (more characters, less convergence) and provides a real example (whales and hippos)". Both failing spans are recovered, pre-existing text from retired parent APBIO-FRQ-L-025 — not authored by F.
recommended_action: Raise as a grader defect in its own lane, not as content rework. The integrity checker is already detecting these, so production grading_results may carry the same pattern against real attempts — worth querying before any canonical is ratified against this gate.

finding: The QA grader path cannot exercise DECISION-0052's 100% rule on most of the corpus. evaluate-attempt's QA handler returns HTTP 409 canonical_answer_already_present whenever canonical_answer_1 is non-empty, so only items that currently lack a canonical answer can be graded. For Biology that is 7 of 75 published FRQ, and 4 of those are hand-drawn and cannot be graded from text — leaving 3 of F's 71 items, about 4%.
evidence: Verified read-only: 75 published Biology FRQ, 7 with blank canonical_answer_1 (APBIO-FRQ-S-101/102/103 plus the four APBIO-HDG-2026-GRAPH items), 68 blocked by the guard. The guard is in the deployed handler immediately after the content fetch. The same limit applies to every work order B and C item, since all of those either have a canonical already or are the items B authored.
recommended_action: Product Owner decision. The guard is a sensible safety default for the original use case (grade drafts for items with no canonical) but it makes DECISION-0052's gate ceremonial for ~96% of the library. Widening it — for example allowing a caller-supplied answer to be graded against an item that already has a canonical, still under the capability token and still no-persist — is a Production change to a token-gated path and needs authorising.

finding: The deployed evaluate-attempt contains an entire QA subsystem that does not exist in the repository. Production is running code main does not have.
evidence: Deployed evaluate-attempt is version 56, updated 2026-09-22T00:47:19Z. Its source contains handleQaNoPersist, the constant QA_NO_PERSIST_PATH_VERSION = "evaluate-attempt-qa-no-persist-2026-09-22", the x-qa-grader-token check, the verify_qa_grader_token RPC call and the persistence-flags response block. grep across the whole repository returns zero occurrences of qa_no_persist, x-qa-grader-token or qa_grader. The supporting database objects app.qa_grade_frq and app.verify_qa_grader_token likewise exist in Production.
recommended_action: Commit the deployed source. This is the same class as the 160 local-only files found on 2026-09-22: code that produces live behaviour while its source sits outside the repository, so it cannot be reviewed, diffed or rolled back. The QA path is well built — token-gated, no-persist, documented in its own docstring — which makes it more worth capturing, not less.
